zh.title: 華盛頓杜勒斯機場200億美元重建計畫　旅客費或漲至90美元
zh.summary: 華盛頓杜勒斯機場（IAD）擬推200億美元重建；旅客費用估自13美元漲至90美元。
body: 在一項高達200億美元的華盛頓杜勒斯國際機場重建計畫中，旅客費用可能面臨大幅調升。根據規劃內容，該機場的旅客費用可能會從目前的13美元急劇飆升至90美元。
這項重建計畫的核心內容包含拆除華盛頓杜勒斯國際機場現有的設施與建築，並預計新建一座名為「川普航廈」（Trump Terminal）的全新設施。
在200億美元重建方案的影響下，行經華盛頓杜勒斯國際機場的旅客費用將出現大幅變動，從原本每人13美元收費水準大幅提升至90美元。
該項計畫詳細列出了拆除華盛頓杜勒斯國際機場現有設施並新建川普航廈對消費者所產生的成本與費用影響。

en.title: Dulles Airport $20 Billion Rebuild Plan Could See Passenger Fees Rise To $90
en.summary: Washington Dulles Airport (IAD) proposes a $20 billion rebuild; passenger fees could soar from $13 to $90.
body: Passenger fees at Washington Dulles International Airport  could soar from $13 to $90 under a proposed $20 billion rebuild plan for the airport facility.

The financial details outline the consumer cost associated with plans to tear down existing infrastructure at Washington Dulles International Airport and build a new facility designated as the 'Trump Terminal.'
Under the $20 billion rebuild proposal, charges for passengers utilizing Washington Dulles International Airport would increase from the current rate of $13 to $90 per passenger.
The project details the consumer impact of replacing current IAD infrastructure with the proposed 'Trump Terminal' structure as part of the overall $20 billion redevelopment.

zh.title: FAA將空管網路現代化移交AT&T，首筆7430萬美元標案啟動
zh.summary: FAA將FENS空管通訊網路移轉至AT&T；首筆7430萬美元；Verizon轉支援角色
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）將其空管網路現代化計畫的關鍵部分移交AT&T，向該公司發放一筆7430萬美元的初始合約，此合約預期將成長為數十億美元規模的交易。
此標案涵蓋FAA企業網路服務（FENS）的初期工作。FENS是支援FAA更廣泛的美國空管系統翻新計畫的通訊網路，旨在取代已運作逾二十年的FAA電信基礎設施網路，該網路連接空管設施與全國空域系統中的其他FAA作業。
FAA先前於2023年曾將一份為期15年、價值超過20億美元的FENS合約授予Verizon，由Verizon負責設計、建造、營運與維護下一代通訊平台。新的AT&T標案則是在FAA加速推動「全新空管系統」計畫之際推出，該計畫目標是在2028年底前取代老舊的雷達、電信、軟體與硬體。
FAA表示，正圍繞AT&T重組FENS以加速部署並趕上2028年空管現代化期限，Verizon將維持支援角色。電信是該計畫最高優先事項之一，因為它連接整個國家空域系統。FAA指出，已將超過三分之一的老舊銅線基礎設施更換為高速數位光纖。
更廣泛的現代化計畫需要5,170條使用光纖、衛星與無線技術的新高速網路連線，另包括27,625部新無線電、462台數位語音交換機與612座新雷達。FAA表示，此工程旨在提升可靠性並減少因老舊設備造成的延誤。根據該機構資料，2025年因設備問題導致的航班延誤分鐘數較2010至2024年平均值高出約300%。
美國國會已為空管翻新計畫撥款125億美元，但FAA表示尚需另外200億美元才能完成整個計畫。FAA尚未公布AT&T長期FENS協議的完整金額，7430萬美元的初始標案是新安排下首批公開確認的資助工作，預期將在數年內大幅成長。

en.title: FAA shifts air traffic network overhaul to AT&T with initial $74.3 million award
en.summary: FAA moves FENS communications network to AT&T; initial $74.3 million award; Verizon shifts to supporting role
body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has moved a key part of its air traffic control network modernization effort to AT&T, awarding the company an initial $74.3 million award under a contract expected to grow into a multibillion-dollar deal.

The award covers initial work on FAA Enterprise Network Services, or FENS, the communications network that will support the agency's broader overhaul of the US air traffic control system. FENS is intended to replace the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure network that has supported agency communications for more than two decades, providing the backbone connecting air traffic facilities and other FAA operations across the National Airspace System.

The FAA previously awarded Verizon a 15-year FENS contract in 2023 worth more than $2 billion, calling for Verizon to design, build, operate and maintain the agency's next-generation communications platform. The new AT&T award comes as the FAA accelerates work on its Brand New Air Traffic Control System, an effort to replace aging radar, telecommunications, software and hardware by the end of 2028.

The FAA said it is restructuring FENS around AT&T to accelerate deployment and meet its 2028 ATC modernization deadline, with Verizon remaining in a supporting role. Telecommunications is one of the highest priorities in that program because it connects the National Airspace System, according to the agency, which says it has already replaced more than one-third of its old copper infrastructure with high-speed digital fiber.

The broader modernization plan calls for 5,170 new high-speed network connections using fiber, satellite and wireless technology, along with 27,625 new radios, 462 digital voice switches and 612 new radars. The FAA says the work is aimed at improving reliability and reducing delays caused by aging equipment, noting that flight-delay minutes attributed to equipment problems in 2025 were about 300% higher than the average from 2010 through 2024.

Congress has provided $12.5 billion toward the air traffic control overhaul, but the FAA says another $20 billion will be needed to complete the program. The FAA has not yet disclosed the full value of the long-term AT&T FENS agreement; the initial $74.3 million award is the first publicly identified funded work under the new arrangement but is certain to grow much larger over several years.
